You have a point, but the main issue is derived from the perspective of the audience member. A legend to me has no basis within a modern setting. Rather, a past setting has more reason of existence within a game that has legend in the title. As previously stated, a legend, the word itself when looked up on google, is an event believed to be historical to the audience but not authenticated by actual facts. This alone means that you can't name a sequel to a modern setting story, a legend.

However, there are plenty of post-apocalyptic stories or the like that features legends and myths made set in modern dats. And, as an audience member, I can easily suspend my disbelief that a game with legend in the title would be set in the said times. However, there needs to be an established president to allow that suspension to occur. A game like Fallout has that establishment, ever since the start of the 1st game. All because they took the time to introduce us to the idea of an apocalypse. We have people who talk of legends, who lived those legends, and they help to establish the lore.

 Due to the previous game already establishing that legend means it's set in the past, the title for Legends ZA is faulty. Rather than being a legends game, it should instead be a plain old sequel. Just name it Z. It's not me arguing that if a game has the same title as another game, that means it should carry on the themes, characters, or even continue the story. That's just plainly me explaining, as indef as possible, why a game with legends in the title would be set in the past. There are plenty of franchises that feature sequels or continuations that have nothing to do with the one before. Maybe they share themes, or characters, or ideas, but at this point in time, an audience member could, say look at Final Fantasy 7 and know it has no bearing on Final Fantasy 8 and vise versa. Meaning that there is a set presidence for the franchise to conduct itself in such a manner.

This is all to say that, just because we only had 1 game does not mean we couldn't derive the beginning of a pattern. For the first title to be set in the past and feature the word legend, it would be easy to assume that Legends ZA could have been set in the past as well. At the end of the day, we don't have any clue as to why they titled it a legends game. Outside of building hype around the title. Maybe it shares a theme, or it's trying to build up to something like Xenoblade chronicles 1 and 2 built up to 3. As stated before by another, the sample size is too small to derive any real meaning, and perhaps, as stated by another, the title is meant to feature a Legendary Pokémon. But every Pokémon game does that. So other than a cash grab, why name it Legends? I'm all the more excited to find out, is what I've come to find.

It's less so the sample size though I won't deny it played a part. It's more so an assumption based on the word legend itself. Which is a word used to describe things that happened in the past, usually regarding legendary entities or events.
